From 921c0f5ba58e4064deb18b4985a202508fc5527f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Parav Pandit <parav@mellanox.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Jul 2018 13:40:30 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] IB/mlx5: Honor cnt_set_id_valid flag instead of set_id

It is incorrect to depend on set_id value to know if counters were
allocated or not. set_id_valid field is set to true when counters
were allocated. Therefore, use set_id_valid while deciding to
free counters.

Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> # 4.15
Fixes: aac4492ef23a ("IB/mlx5: Update counter implementation for dual port RoCE")
Signed-off-by: Parav Pandit <parav@mellanox.com>
Reviewed-by: Daniel Jurgens <danielj@mellanox.com>
Signed-off-by: Leon Romanovsky <leonro@mellanox.com>
Signed-off-by: Jason Gunthorpe <jgg@mellanox.com>

diff --git a/drivers/infiniband/hw/mlx5/main.c b/drivers/infiniband/hw/mlx5/main.c
index f86b5ad2dd43..0f482d2a760f 100644
--- a/drivers/infiniband/hw/mlx5/main.c
+++ b/drivers/infiniband/hw/mlx5/main.c
@@ -4699,7 +4699,7 @@ static void mlx5_ib_dealloc_counters(struct mlx5_ib_dev *dev)
 	int i;
 
 	for (i = 0; i < dev->num_ports; i++) {
-		if (dev->port[i].cnts.set_id)
+		if (dev->port[i].cnts.set_id_valid)
 			mlx5_core_dealloc_q_counter(dev->mdev,
 						    dev->port[i].cnts.set_id);
 		kfree(dev->port[i].cnts.names);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/infiniband/hw/mlx5/main.c`**
   - The condition used to check if counters should be deallocated has been changed. 
   - The original line:
     ```c
     if (dev->port[i].cnts.set_id)
     ```
     has been modified to:
     ```c
     if (dev->port[i].cnts.set_id_valid)
     ```
   - This change ensures that the code now checks the `set_id_valid` flag instead of the `set_id` value to determine if counters were allocated.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `main.c` directly addresses a logical error in the counter deallocation process. By switching from using `set_id` to `set_id_valid`, the code now correctly identifies whether counters were allocated based on the validity flag, rather than relying on the potentially misleading `set_id` value. This change improves the reliability of the counter management in the driver, ensuring that resources are only freed when they have been properly allocated.

Here is the commit message:
IB/mlx5: Honor cnt_set_id_valid flag instead of set_id

It is incorrect to depend on set_id value to know if counters were
allocated or not. set_id_valid field is set to true when counters
were allocated. Therefore, use set_id_valid while deciding to
free counters.

Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> # 4.15
Fixes: aac4492ef23a ("IB/mlx5: Update counter implementation for dual port RoCE")
Signed-off-by: Parav Pandit <parav@mellanox.com>
Reviewed-by: Daniel Jurgens <danielj@mellanox.com>
Signed-off-by: Leon Romanovsky <leonro@mellanox.com>
Signed-off-by: Jason Gunthorpe <jgg@mellanox.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug arises from incorrectly relying on the `set_id` value to determine if counters were allocated, rather than using the `set_id_valid` flag. This could lead to attempts to deallocate counters that were not actually allocated, potentially causing resource management issues and memory leaks.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void mlx5_ib_dealloc_counters(struct mlx5_ib_dev *dev)
 {
 	int i;
 
 	for (i = 0; i < dev->num_ports; i++) {
-		if (dev->port[i].cnts.set_id)
+		if (dev->port[i].cnts.set_id_valid)
 			mlx5_core_dealloc_q_counter(dev->mdev,
 						    dev->port[i].cnts.set_id);
 		kfree(dev->port[i].cnts.names);
 		kfree(dev->port[i].cnts.offsets);
 	}
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c

```
Reason:
This statement incorrectly checks the `set_id` value to determine if counters were allocated. If `set_id` is non-zero, it assumes that counters are allocated, which is not always true. This can lead to attempts to deallocate counters that were never allocated, causing resource management issues.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (dev->port[i].cnts.set_id_valid)
```
Reason:
This statement correctly checks the `set_id_valid` flag, which is set to true when counters are actually allocated. By using this flag, the code ensures that it only attempts to deallocate counters that were allocated, thus preventing potential memory leaks and resource mismanagement.
